finding: On Windows a read-only target leaves its temp file behind, and a cleanup PermissionError replaces the SafeWriteError.
why: The temp file is set read-only (S_IMODE of a 0o444 target) before the swap; os.replace onto a read-only file is denied on every retry, then `temporary.unlink` in the finally block is denied too, so the docstring promise that a refusal deletes the temp file breaks and the caller gets `[WinError 5] Access is denied: '.ro.txt.<hex>.tmp'` with the real refusal only as __context__ (scratchpad probe: target chmod 0o444, update_locked -> PermissionError, ctx SafeWriteError('file swap stayed busy'), leftover ['.ro.txt.67522c93f1fd.tmp'], content unchanged).
fix: Apply the target mode only after a successful swap, or clear the read-only bit (os.chmod(temporary, stat.S_IWRITE|stat.S_IREAD)) before unlink in the finally block, and do not retry a denied replace as if the swap were busy.
evidence:
+        if mode is not None:
+            os.chmod(temporary, mode)  ... finally: ... temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True); docstring: "A refusal or failure deletes the temp file and leaves the file unchanged."

finding: The new refusal names the resolved real file, not the caller's path, and the module docstring's list of refusals does not mention it.
why: Every other SafeWriteError names `target` (the tests check caught.value.path == target), so for a symlinked instruction file this one path reports a different file; the docstring at lines 8-11 lists the refusals (lock held, file changed, busy replace) and is now incomplete (FRESHNESS.md 'no artifact goes stale').
fix: Pass `target` into _open_temporary and raise SafeWriteError("no free temp file name", target); add the case to the docstring's list of refusals.
evidence: raise SafeWriteError("no free temp file name", write_target)

finding: The test name claims 'creates nothing', but the safe writer's lock takes `.target.md.afk.lock` in tmp_path before the stat fails, and the test checks only the target.
why: The name promises more than the asserts check, and the stderr check accepts any message with the prefix, so a different OSError (not the missing target) would pass too.
fix: Rename to 'creates no target', or assert the folder holds only source.md and the lock file; also assert the stderr message names the target path.

finding: The test named 'closed exactly once' cannot catch a leaked temp descriptor, only a second explicit close.
why: track_descriptors records only explicit os.close calls, and the file object from os.fdopen closes its descriptor in C without calling os.close; so if the handle never closed the descriptor (for example os.fdopen(..., closefd=False)), POSIX gives opened=[t, d], closed=[d] and Windows gives opened=[t], closed=[], and in both cases 0 == 1 - 1 passes; the formula also works only because the directory descriptor may or may not reuse the temp descriptor's number.
fix: Wrap os.fdopen to keep the returned handle and assert handle.closed after the call, plus closed.count(temp_descriptor) == 0 when no number reuse happened; or rename the test to 'never closed a second time'.

finding: Possible weak mode check: the new-file mode assertion runs under the ambient umask, so a hard-coded 0o644 create mode survives on a typical umask 022 runner; the assert also sits behind an if inside the test body.
why: With umask 022, 0o666 & ~umask equals 0o644, so the test cannot tell the umask-respecting DEFAULT_CREATE_MODE path from a fixed mode, and the in-body os.name branch hides the skip on Windows.
fix: Set a distinctive umask (e.g. 0o027) before the call and restore it in a finally, then expect 0o640; move the mode check into a separate POSIX-only test with skipif instead of the in-body if.
